recreation_prompt_markdown:
Create a polished single-screen browser arcade game called **Checkpoint Rope Run** where the player controls one highlighted runner standing in the center of a neon obstacle arena. The only action should be jumping: the player can tap or click the playfield on mobile/desktop, or press **Space** / **Up Arrow**, to leap over a rotating sweep rope that circles the arena. Structure the experience as a quick replayable score attack with a start screen, an in-game HUD, and a game-over screen with instant restart.

Render the game on a full-screen HTML5 canvas with a glossy neon-purple, magenta, and mint presentation. The arena should feel like a futuristic game-show lane with glowing floor streaks, subtle animated background pulses, and a luminous rope that visibly passes behind and then in front of the runners as it rotates. The player character should stand out from the crowd with brighter colors and a small heroic silhouette, while four nearby AI runners act as companions/rivals in the same lane.

The gameplay loop should be simple and readable: the rope rotates continuously, becomes dangerous only when it swings low across the foreground, and the player must jump at the correct moment to avoid being clipped while grounded. Use fixed jump physics with gravity and a single jump impulse, no double-jump, and no lateral movement. The round should end immediately if the player is still on the ground when the low front rope reaches them. Award **one checkpoint** every time the rope completes a full safe rotation while the player remains alive.

Add four AI runners that auto-jump with imperfect timing so some survive for a while and others get knocked out as the speed increases. Show the remaining number of living runners in the HUD to create a last-runner-standing atmosphere, even though the player’s main goal is personal survival and score. Gradually increase the rope speed throughout the run so the timing window tightens and tension rises naturally.

Include juicy feedback: looping arcade background music, distinct sound effects for start, jump, landing, checkpoint gain, AI runner elimination, and game over. Use celebratory visual feedback when the player scores and a dramatic failure reaction overlay when the run ends. Keep the UI mobile-safe with compact top HUD pills, centered modal cards for start and restart, and a clean readable arcade font treatment. The final result should feel like a neon jump-rope survival minigame: easy to understand instantly, fast to replay, and increasingly intense the longer the player lasts.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## High-level code structure
- Single-file browser game contained entirely in `index.html`.
- Three main layers coexist in the document:
  - **Presentation layer:** CSS-driven neon arcade styling, HUD pills, modal start/game-over cards, and animated feedback GIF overlays.
  - **Playfield layer:** A full-screen HTML5 `<canvas>` used for all gameplay rendering.
  - **Logic/audio layer:** Inline JavaScript initializes assets, audio helpers, state objects, input bindings, rendering, and the frame loop.
- The code is organized procedurally around a small set of stateful functions rather than modules or components.

## Game loop / state model
- Boot flow:
  - `DOMContentLoaded` wires up DOM references, audio, resize handling, and input.
  - `resize()` fits the canvas to the viewport and repositions the player and AI runners.
  - `draw()` renders an idle preview before the round begins.
- Round flow:
  - Start button unlocks audio, hides the start card, shows the HUD, calls `initGame()`, then starts `gameLoop()`.
  - `initGame()` resets score, rope rotation speed/angle, player state, and four AI bot runners.
  - `gameLoop()` runs only while `gameActive` is true, calling `update()` then `draw()` every animation frame.
- Stateful variables:
  - **Global run state:** `gameActive`, `score`, `frameCount`.
  - **Rope state:** `ropeAngle`, `ropeSpeed`, `ropeRadius`, `ropeCenterY`.
  - **Player state:** position, vertical velocity, grounded/dead flags, body dimensions, color.
  - **Bot state:** same physical fields plus light AI variance (`reactionDelay`, `failChance`, though these are only partially used).
- End state:
  - If the low rope reaches the player while grounded, `gameOver()` stops the run, stops BGM, plays fail SFX, reveals the result card, and freezes progression.
  - Restart reinitializes the same round structure from scratch.

## Player goals
- Time jumps so the player clears the sweeping rope whenever it passes at low height in the foreground.
- Survive as many rope rotations as possible.
- Accumulate score through completed rope cycles, labeled as **checkpoints cleared**.
- Implicit secondary goal: outlast the AI crowd as other runners get clipped and eliminated.

## Interaction pattern
- Primary interaction is **single-action timing input**:
  - Mouse/tap on the canvas
  - Space bar
  - Up arrow
- Each valid input triggers a jump only if the player is grounded and alive.
- No directional movement, aiming, inventory, or menu depth beyond start/restart.
- Failure condition is binary and immediate: being on the ground when the rope sweeps through the danger zone.

## Core systems
- **Jump physics:** gravity plus a fixed jump impulse create a readable arc.
- **Rotating obstacle system:** a simulated rope rotates using sine/cosine; the code distinguishes front/back phases and only threatens the player when the rope is low and in front.
- **Scoring system:** score increments once per completed rope revolution if the player is still alive.
- **AI crowd system:** four bot runners auto-jump with imperfect timing and can be eliminated individually.
- **HUD system:** live checkpoint counter and total surviving runners.
- **Audio feedback system:** looping BGM plus SFX for start, jump, landing, scoring, failures, and bot knockouts.
- **Visual feedback system:** neon lane rendering, highlighted main runner, feedback GIFs for scoring and failure, and modal overlays for round transitions.
- **Responsive/mobile-safe presentation:** fullscreen layout, safe-area padding, tap-focused canvas input, compact HUD scaling.

## Inferred genre / gameplay shape
- Closest shape is a **single-screen timing/avoidance arcade game**.
- It behaves like a reflex-based **rope-jump survival runner** with endless-score escalation rather than level-based progression.
- The “checkpoint” framing and ever-faster rope give it a light endless-runner feel, but mechanically it is more about **reaction timing against a cyclical hazard** than forward movement.
- It also carries a small **last-runner-standing spectacle** through the presence of AI runners dropping out over time.

## Gameplay heuristic
- Watch the rope’s approach phase and jump late enough to avoid getting clipped while still airborne over the low sweep.
- Because rope speed gradually increases, the timing window tightens over time and pushes the session from casual rhythm into high-pressure reflex play.
- The bots serve as atmosphere and comparative performance cues; their eliminations reinforce survival pressure and communicate that the player is enduring longer than the crowd.

## Confidence notes
- High confidence on the core loop, scoring, failure rule, and input model because all of these are explicit in code.
- Medium confidence on thematic framing beyond “neon rope-run arena,” since no narrative text exists beyond UI flavor strings.
- Medium confidence on genre labeling because the game combines endless survival, obstacle timing, and runner aesthetics in a very compact form.

The action occurs on a fixed ground lane with timing-based avoidance rather than free movement, so it resembles a stationary lane-style runner focused on obstacle clearance.
Success depends on repeatedly timing a single action to a cyclical sweep pattern, giving the game a rhythm-like cadence even though there are no beat charts or note tracks.
The escalating rope speed increases pressure and demands faster reactions, which partially aligns with speed-runner reflex gameplay.
The player endures repeated incoming sweeps while other runners get removed over time, loosely echoing wave survival despite lacking combat or defense structures.
